video.title: The Most Overlooked $10K/M Business Anyone Can Start

summary: Chris Koerner interviews 23-year-old Kyler, who rents used washers and dryers to renters via Facebook Marketplace in Utah, claiming about $10K/month with 120+ sets, no employees and 5-10 hours a week. His 'Post, Rent, Buy' process validates demand with a listing before buying any machines. Used Whirlpool direct-drive sets are sourced free or cheap, and he also covers appliance delivery for used-appliance shops as a side income. The video ends with a plug for Kyler's paid school community and Chris's TK Owners community.

ideas.name: Washer and dryer rental via Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Rent used washer/dryer sets monthly to renters at $60-85, installed free, and get paid by card subscription.
ideas.business_model: Monthly recurring rental subscription with free delivery, install and maintenance
ideas.customer: Renters in apartments and houses without a washer and dryer, who would otherwise use a laundromat
ideas.problem: Tenants lack in-unit laundry and laundromats are inconvenient and costly
ideas.offer: Month-to-month washer and dryer rental, free delivery, install and maintenance, minimum 6 months

pricing.model: Monthly subscription per set; used $60, new $85
pricing.notes: Lists at $60 on Marketplace; first payment due on install day. Customers described as not price sensitive.

acquisition_channels.details: Posts 'washer and dryer for rent' on Facebook Marketplace with real-looking photos, multiple accounts with different zip codes, and shares into local groups. The rental title breaks the pattern among 'for sale' listings. Fast replies (same day) are critical, using saved message templates. Pays $12/month for the verified badge to get support when banned.

quote.text: they're going to see washer and dryer $60. They're going to click it. they're never seen something for rent. It breaks their pattern.
quote.speaker: Kyler

acquisition_channels.details: Hangs door hangers on apartment complexes known not to provide laundry; 30 minutes per 200 doors, 3-4 leads per complex. Ordered 10,000 at about 5 cents each, expecting 1-3% response.
Word of mouth and long-lived customers; some customers keep sets for 1.5 years.

ideas.delivery: Kyler (with his younger brother) hauls sets in a small trailer behind a Toyota Highlander, installs in 30-45 minutes, tests, has the customer sign a contract and shows them how to use it. Service calls run 5-8 per month, some solved by phone. Removes sets on move-out, pressure washes, and re-rents in 2-3 days. Repairs use parts harvested from scrap machines.
unit_economics_claims: Used sets cost $0-$200, payback in 4-5 months
About 50 churned of about 170 delivered over about 24 months (about 1.5%/month)
ideas.startup_cost: Can be $0 using free machines. Kyler spent about $3,000 on three new sets at RC Willey and then $30,000 with wholesalers, about half his life savings or more in the first month. Used sets cost $0-$200, or about $300 with a warranty.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First install 15 Nov 2023, a day after a lead confirmed; first payment due on install day

acquisition.how: Marketplace posting and message replies could be agent-assisted but Meta limits automation and multi-account tactics risk bans; door hangers are physical.

onboarding.how: Contract signing and a demo happen in person at install; lead qualification and scheduling could be automated.

delivery.how: Hauling, installing, repairing and removing machines is physical and cannot be automated.

billing.how: Stripe subscriptions charge cards automatically each month.

support.how: Agents could triage phone troubleshooting (e.g. lint-blocked vents) but repairs need a visit.

uk_applicability.notes: Rental model could work for UK renters without machines, and Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree exist. However, UK homes typically use a front-load washing machine (often with no separate dryer or vent), top-load Whirlpool direct-drive units are rare, and landlords often supply machines. Rental and consumer law, electrical safety and insurance need checking.

risks: Facebook account bans, especially with multiple accounts
Non-binding contract; no legal protection initially
Fire risk from lint-blocked dryer vents

tactics.name: Post, Rent, Buy validation
steps: Post a rental listing with a realistic photo before owning inventory
Reply to every enquirer quickly and confirm interest
Once a customer commits, buy the machines and install
Scale only when demand is proven

quote.text: I call it the PRB process. Step one, post it. Okay. Step two, rent it. Okay. Step three, buy it.
quote.speaker: Kyler

tactics.name: Marketplace listing recipe
steps: Title 'Washer and dryer for rent'
Price $60 and use many photos of real machines
Description: 'Never go to the laundromat again. Rent a washer and dryer month-to-month, free delivery, install and maintenance'
Post to multiple accounts with different zip codes and into local groups
Use saved reply templates stating $60 used, $85 new, 6-month minimum
Pay the $12/month badge for support

tactics.name: Sourcing free or cheap machines
steps: Search Marketplace for 'free appliances' and 'broken appliances' and message first
Do deliveries for used appliance stores and take trade-ins
Befriend used-appliance sellers who list often and negotiate a bulk deal with a 2-year guarantee
Get scrappers to send daily pictures and drop off units
Give delivery drivers your number so they offer removed units for about $15-20 each
Part out a dead unit to repair others

tactics.name: Door-hanger campaign on apartment complexes
steps: Pick complexes where a rented set already proves no laundry is provided
Hang flyers on all doors (about 30 minutes per 200 doors)
Expect 3-4 leads per complex
Print in bulk at about 5 cents each

tactics.name: Install and onboarding script
steps: Check the layout and test water and dryer
Have the customer sign the contract and state it is rental not rent-to-own
Explain free maintenance and card auto-charge on a fixed day
Give a 2-minute usage demo, load limits and lint trap guidance
Take card details on the spot

tactics.name: Automate recurring billing with Stripe
steps: Move from Cash App to Stripe subscriptions
Charge cards automatically each month to avoid chasing payments

tools_mentioned.name: Ryobi drill and channel locks
tools_mentioned.purpose: Only tools needed for install and repair

warnings.warning: Slow response on Marketplace loses leads; reply within the same day.

quote.text: If you don't respond quick, like within the same day, then they're going to say, "Oh, actually, I found one or I decided to do something else."

warnings.warning: He ran without insurance for 3 months and used a non-binding Google Docs contract.
Buying new machines was a costly mistake; renters just want a working unit.

lessons.lesson: Validate demand with a listing before spending on inventory; the downside is only wasted time.
A boring, year-round niche rental (in-home appliance) beat seasonal rentals like boats and paddle boards.

quote.text: washers and dryers, they all year round. And it stays in their house.
quote.speaker: Kyler

lessons.lesson: Recurring rental revenue with low churn (about 1.5%/month) is driven by leases and convenience.
Cheaper used inventory was just as attractive as new, so cost cuts barely hurt demand.
Build supplier relationships (shops, drivers, scrappers) for steady cheap inventory.
Automate payments early (Stripe) to remove admin as you scale.
Fast response and a pattern-breaking listing title beat polish in marketplace selling.
Resourcefulness over capital: rent a truck or hitch rather than buying one.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific process details and numbers, but revenue and churn are unverified verbal claims and the interview is friendly and promotional; the headline $10K/month is stated by the host, not independently shown.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Kyler sells a paid school community; Chris Koerner promotes TK Owners community.

extraction.review_notes: The extraction is thorough and accurate on the core washer/dryer rental model, the sourcing tactics, the listing recipe and the promotional conflicts. Errors are small: one non-verbatim quote, an invented time-to-first-revenue detail, a misattributed insurance claim, and a slightly inaccurate UK note. The early recreational rentals were missed as a minor idea, and a few second-hand scale claims (Burley friend, the 900-set operator) were not captured as metric claims.
